2: 'use strict';
3: /**
4:  * add-pair — create or repair an account, and keep an access code and its
5:  * auth password in step.
6:  *
7:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com            # generates a code
8:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com 24681000   # or you choose it (8+ digits)
9:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js someone@sage.com --remove    # take access away
10:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js --list                      # who has access
11:  *   node tooling/add-pair.js --selftest                  # offline, no network
12:  *
13:  * WHY A COMMAND AND NOT AN ADMIN PAGE
14:  * Creating the Supabase account and moving its password need the service_role
15:  * key. Put that in a browser and it is in the page for anyone to read — the
16:  * service_role bypasses RLS entirely, so leaking it is leaking the table. A
17:  * command keeps the master key on one machine.
18:  *
19:  * WHERE THE PAIRS LIVE (since 2026-10-14)
20:  * public.quick_signin_accounts, verified through resolve_pair(email, code).
21:  * The admin edits rows in the comment panel (Reviewer tab -> Access) and those
22:  * edits apply immediately; nothing in this repo holds a code any more. This
23:  * tool writes the same row, plus the one thing the panel cannot do: create the
24:  * auth account or move its password.
25:  *
26:  * THE CODE IS THE ACCOUNT PASSWORD
27:  * Deliberate: the sign-in paths hand the pair straight to signInWithPassword
28:  * (or signUp on first use), so a separate secret would be a second thing to
29:  * keep in sync for no gain. resolve_pair verifies the pairing; Supabase
30:  * verifies the password.
31:  *
32:  * THE BOT ID IS WHY THE PASSWORD MOVE EXISTS
33:  * The id `bot` (typed where an email goes) signs in as bot@sage.com, a real
34:  * account, so it can comment. Changing its code in the panel changes the ROW
35:  * immediately — the gate and middleware re-resolve it — but the ACCOUNT
36:  * password is only moved here:
37:  *
38:  *   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=... node tooling/add-pair.js bot@sage.com <new code>
39:  *
40:  * on the host that holds the key. Until then the pair resolves but sign-in
41:  * refuses, which is the safe direction.
42:  */
43: 
44: const fs = require('fs');
45: 
46: const DEFAULT_URL = 'https://ltyyzxnxufvkorekglrf.supabase.co';
47: const TABLE = '/rest/v1/quick_signin_accounts';
48: const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
49: const has = f => argv.includes(f);
50: const val = (f, d) => { const i = argv.indexOf(f); return i === -1 ? d : argv[i + 1]; };
51: 
52: const isEmail = s => /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(s);
53: 
54: function makeCode() {
55:   // 10 digits from crypto, not Math.random. Readable aloud over a call, and
56:   // long enough that it is not worth guessing. (5 bytes keeps the value under
57:   // 2^53 so the modulo does not lose precision.)
58:   const c = require('crypto').randomBytes(5).readUIntBE(0, 5) % 10000000000;
59:   return String(c).padStart(10, '0');
60: }
61: 
62: // Pure paths, kept small so --selftest can cover them offline. PostgREST wants
63: // the filter value URL-encoded, or a plus-tag in an address becomes a space.
64: const listPath = () => TABLE + '?select=email,code&order=email.asc';
65: const filterPath = (email, select) => TABLE + '?'
66:   + (select ? 'select=email,code&' : '')
67:   + 'email=eq.' + encodeURIComponent(email);
68: const upsertPath = () => TABLE + '?on_conflict=email';
69: 
70: // ------------------------------------------------------------------ supabase --
71: 
72: function serviceKey() {
73:   if (process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) return process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;
74:   const f = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE;
75:   if (f && fs.existsSync(f)) {
76:     const m = /^\s*(?:SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\s*=\s*)?(\S+)\s*$/.exec(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
77:     if (m) return m[1];
78:   }
79:   return null;
80: }
81: 
82: async function api(base, key, method, path_, body, extraHeaders) {
83:   const res = await fetch(`${base}${path_}`, {
84:     method,
85:     headers: Object.assign(
86:       { apikey: key, Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
87:       extraHeaders || {},
88:     ),
89:     body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),
90:   });
91:   const text = await res.text();
92:   let json = null;
93:   try { json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null; } catch (e) { /* not json */ }
94:   if (!res.ok) {
95:     const why = (json && (json.msg || json.message || json.error_description)) || `HTTP ${res.status}`;
96:     throw new Error(why);
97:   }
98:   return json;
99: }
100: 
101: /** Create the user, or reset the password if it already exists. */
102: async function upsertUser(base, key, email, password) {
103:   const list = await api(base, key, 'GET', '/auth/v1/admin/users?per_page=200');
104:   const hit = (list.users || []).find(u => (u.email || '').toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase());
105:   if (!hit) {
106:     await api(base, key, 'POST', '/auth/v1/admin/users', { email, password, email_confirm: true });
107:     return 'created';
108:   }
109:   await api(base, key, 'PUT', `/auth/v1/admin/users/${hit.id}`, { password, email_confirm: true });
110:   return 'password reset';
111: }
112: 
113: // -------------------------------------------------------------------- main ---
114: 
115: async function main() {
116:   if (has('--selftest')) return selftest();
117: 
118:   const key = serviceKey();
119:   if (!key) {
120:     console.error('  no SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, and no SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE readable.');
121:     console.error('  the pairs live in Supabase now, so this tool always needs the service');
122:     console.error('  key — the panel (Reviewer tab -> Access) is the keyless editor.');
123:     process.exitCode = 1;
124:     return;
125:   }
126:   const base = val('--url', process.env.SUPABASE_URL || DEFAULT_URL);
127: 
128:   if (has('--list')) {
129:     const rows = await api(base, key, 'GET', listPath());
130:     console.log('  ' + (rows.length ? 'ids with quick sign-in:' : 'nobody yet'));
131:     for (const r of rows) console.log(`    ${r.email}  code ${r.code}`);
132:     return;
133:   }
134: 
135:   const email = val('--email', argv.find(a => !a.startsWith('--')) || '');
136:   if (!email || !isEmail(email)) {
137:     console.error('  usage: node tooling/add-pair.js <email> [code] [--remove]');
138:     console.error('         node tooling/add-pair.js --list | --selftest');
139:     console.error('  needs SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (or SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY_FILE).');
140:     process.exitCode = 1;
141:     return;
142:   }
143:   const lower = email.toLowerCase();
144: 
145:   if (has('--remove')) {
146:     await api(base, key, 'DELETE', filterPath(lower, false));
147:     console.log(`  removed ${lower}`);
148:     console.log('  an auth account (if any) stays; with no row, resolve_pair refuses its pair.');
149:     return;
150:   }
151: 
152:   const code = val('--code', argv.find(a => /^\d{8,}$/.test(a))) || makeCode();
153:   await api(base, key, 'POST', upsertPath(), { email: lower, code }, { Prefer: 'resolution=merge-duplicates' });
154:   const how = await upsertUser(base, key, lower, code);
155:   console.log(`  paired ${lower}`);
156:   console.log(`  code:   ${code}`);
157:   console.log(`  user:   ${how}`);
158: }
159: 
160: // ---------------------------------------------------------------- selftest ---
161: 
162: function selftest() {
163:   let pass = 0, fail = 0;
164:   const t = (n, got, want) => {
165:     const a = JSON.stringify(got), b = JSON.stringify(want);
166:     if (a === b) { pass++; console.log(`  ok    ${n}`); }
167:     else { fail++; console.log(`  FAIL  ${n}\n          got  ${a}\n          want ${b}`); }
168:   };
169: 
170:   console.log('paths the REST calls use');
171:   t('the list asks for both columns, ordered', listPath(),
172:     TABLE + '?select=email,code&order=email.asc');
173:   t('a filtered read selects the columns too', filterPath('a@sage.com', true),
174:     TABLE + '?select=email,code&email=eq.a%40sage.com');
175:   t('a filter encodes a plus-tag, not a space', filterPath('a+bot@sage.com', false),
176:     TABLE + '?email=eq.a%2Bbot%40sage.com');
177:   t('the upsert says which column decides', upsertPath(), TABLE + '?on_conflict=email');
178: 
179:   console.log('\ninput checking');
180:   t('a real address is accepted', isEmail('someone@sage.com'), true);
181:   t('a missing @ is refused', isEmail('someone.sage.com'), false);
182:   t('an address with a space is refused', isEmail('some one@sage.com'), false);
183: 
184:   console.log('\ngenerated codes');
185:   t('ten digits', /^\d{10}$/.test(makeCode()), true);
186:   t('two in a row differ', makeCode() === makeCode(), false);
187: 
188:   console.log('\n' + pass + ' passed, ' + fail + ' failed');
189:   process.exit(fail ? 1 : 0);
190: }
191: 
192: if (has('--selftest')) selftest();
193: else main().catch(e => { console.error('  ' + e.message); process.exitCode = 1; });
194: 
195: module.exports = { isEmail, makeCode, listPath, filterPath, upsertPath };

2: // /bot poller — hands a page comment to a Health-tracker agent.
3: //
4: // WHY A POLLER AND NOT A WEBHOOK
5: // A webhook needs a public endpoint, and this site is static: vercel.json has no
6: // functions and AGENTS.md forbids adding a build step. So a browser cannot push
7: // anywhere. It writes the comment (which it already can) and something with
8: // outbound access comes and gets it. The same reasoning as sync-watch.js, which
9: // polls Figma for the same reason.
10: //
11: // WHERE IT RUNS
12: // On the VM, beside the bots. SSH as ubuntu@51.254.217.163 works and ~/bot-host is
13: // the Health-tracker checkout. It also runs here read-only against the same REST
14: // endpoint, which is how it is tested.
15: //
16: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --once      poll once
17: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --watch     poll every --interval seconds
18: //   node tooling/bot-dispatch.js --selftest  offline, no network
19: //
20: //   add --notify to hand the instruction to the VM bot over Telegram instead of
21: //   filing the card here. See "the notification path" below for why that is the
22: //   default shape to grow toward: it needs no credential off-box, and a human
23: //   sees the instruction. Without --notify this file still does create -> pack ->
24: //   dispatch itself, which is the right thing when it runs beside the bots.
25: //
26: // THE CLAIM IS ATOMIC, AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE
27: // Filing the card is what claims the comment. POST /api/bugs dedupes on title_key,
28: // so `page:<slug> comment:<uuid>` returns 200 {existing:true} for a comment already
29: // filed and creates nothing. That is an atomic conditional write at the store,
30: // which is the whole point of the Idempotent Consumer pattern: a check-then-set in
31: // a poller has a window where two overlapping passes both pass the check.
32: //
33: // The claim is atomic, and it is not in this file. Filing the card is what claims
34: // the comment: the store dedupes on title_key, so `page:<slug> comment:<uuid>`
35: // returns the existing card and creates nothing. That is an atomic conditional
36: // write at the store, which is the whole point of the Idempotent Consumer pattern:
37: // a check-then-set in a poller has a window where two overlapping passes both
38: // pass the check.
39: //
40: //   What I had wrong, and what this now says instead: "create is idempotent" was
41: //   true and useless on its own. `pack` overwrites the defect pack and resets the
42: //   card's state unconditionally, and it is the reset that re-opens the dispatch
43: //   guard — so a poller that re-created and re-packed every recent comment would
44: //   have unblocked a SECOND agent on work already in flight, every five minutes.
45: //   So the store is read once per pass (bugIndex) and a comment whose card is
46: //   already past `packed` is skipped, not re-packed. The card is the record; the
47: //   poller reads it rather than keeping a state file of its own.
48: //
49: //   The trap: `create` alone is not dispatch. run-coding-dispatch.sh --task= is
50: //   refused by packCheck (exit 1) for an unpacked card, and --ticket= refuses a
51: //   card with no defect (exit 3). All four of pack's fields are mandatory.
52: //
53: //   create's RESPONSE is not trustworthy on the existing path: it reports
54: //   public_n 0 and state "new" for a card that is really #58 and in_fix. Only
55: //   bugctl list is believed. That is a bugctl defect, filed as its own card.

58: const fs = require('fs');
59: const path = require('path');
60: const { spawnSync } = require('child_process');
61: const { pathToFileURL } = require('url');
62: 
63: const ROOT = path.join(__dirname, '..');
64: 
65: const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
66: const has = f => argv.includes(f);
67: const val = (f, d) => { const i = argv.indexOf(f); return i === -1 ? d : argv[i + 1]; };

69: const DEFAULT_PAGE = 'customer-payment-services';

71: // -------------------------------------------------------------- the parser --
72: //
73: // MUST match components/page-comments.js parseBot. They drifted once and the
74: // panel announced one agent while the dispatcher posted to another. An `@` is
75: // required before a target, because an optional bare word is greedy: "/bot fix
76: // the second card" would parse target="fix" and eat the first word of every
77: // multi-word instruction.
78: function parseBot(body) {
79:   const text = body || '';
80:   const m = /^\s*\/bot(?:\s+@([a-z0-9_-]+))?\s+([\s\S]+)$/i.exec(text);

82:   if (!m[1] && /^\s*\/bot\s+@/i.test(text)) return null;

86: /**

88:  *
89:  * Two runs of this poller over the same comment produce the same title_key, so the

101:   const where = anchor ? anchor.replace(/^component:/, '') : 'an unanchored element';

103:     component: where,
104:     observed: `A reviewer left a comment on the ${slug} page, anchored to ${where}.`,

106:     criteria:

156:   if (k.startsWith('sb_publishable_')) return false;
157:   if (k.startsWith('sb_secret_')) return true;

273:  * idempotent consumer that trusts that response re-packs a card an agent is

275:  * which is exactly what un-blocks the dispatch guard for a second agent.

288:     return { ok: false, why: `could not read bugctl list: ${r.out.slice(0, 120)}` };
289:   }

291:   for (const row of (rows || [])) {

294:         tag_id: row.tag_id || null,
295:         public_n: row.public_n || null,
296:         state: row.state || row.status || null,
297:         queue: row.queue || null,
298:       });
299:     }
300:   }

304: /**
305:  * create -> pack -> dispatch. All three, in that order.
306:  *
307:  * `create` is idempotent by title_key, so re-running costs nothing. `pack` is the
308:  * one step that is NOT idempotent: POST /api/bugs/:id/defect overwrites item.defect
309:  * unconditionally. It is safe here only because `create` on an already-claimed
310:  * comment returns the EXISTING id and we skip straight to dispatch, whose own PID
311:  * lock refuses a second run.
312:  */
313: function fileAndDispatch(comment, parsed, slug, index) {
314:   const title = claimTitle(slug, comment.id);
315:   const known = index && index.ok ? index.map.get(title) || null : null;
316: 
317:   // THE CLAIM, and the reason this function is safe to run every five minutes.
318:   //
319:   // Read the card BEFORE creating anything. If it is already there and is past
320:   // `packed`, this comment has been dealt with: an agent is on it, or it is
321:   // awaiting verification, or it is done. Re-packing it would overwrite the
322:   // defect pack and reset the state, which is what lets the dispatch guard
323:   // admit a second agent for work already in flight.
324:   if (known) {
325:     return {
326:       stage: 'skip', ok: true, already: known.state,
327:       id: known.tag_id || null, publicN: known.public_n,
328:       why: `already ${known.state || 'filed'} — not re-filed`,
329:     };
330:   }
331: 
332:   const created = bugctl(['create', '--title', title, '--json']);
333:   if (!created.ok) return { stage: 'create', ...created };
334: 
335:   let id = null;
336:   try {
337:     const j = JSON.parse(created.out.slice(created.out.indexOf('{')));
338:     id = j.id || j.tag_id || j.public_n;
339:   } catch (e) { /* fall through to the error below */ }
340:   if (!id) return { stage: 'create', ok: false, why: `could not read an id from: ${created.out.slice(0, 160)}` };
341:   // create's own public_n is unusable (see bugIndex), so the canonical list is
342:   // asked again. One list per pass, not one per comment.
343:   const publicN = index && index.ok && index.map.get(title)
344:     ? index.map.get(title).public_n
345:     : null;
346: 
347:   const f = packFields(parsed, comment.anchor, slug);
348:   const packed = bugctl(['pack', '--id', String(id),
349:     '--component', f.component, '--observed', f.observed,
350:     '--expected', f.expected, '--criteria', f.criteria, '--json']);
351:   if (!packed.ok) return { stage: 'pack', id, ...packed };
352: 
353:   // --foreground is what makes the exit code meaningful: it says whether the
354:   // agent actually started. Under a systemd timer that is the wrong trade —
355:   // Type=oneshot stays "activating" for the whole dispatch, so the unit cannot
356:   // tick again, and a hung dispatch stops the poller entirely. --detach lets go
357:   // and takes the card + the Telegram notice as the signal instead.
358:   const dispatchArgs = [`--ticket=#${id}`];
359:   if (!has('--detach')) dispatchArgs.push('--foreground');
360:   const dispatched = spawnSync('bash',
361:     [path.join(process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'),
362:       'scripts', 'run-coding-dispatch.sh'), ...dispatchArgs],
363:     { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: process.env.BOT_HOST_DIR || path.join(ROOT, '..', 'Health-tracker'), timeout: 900000 });
364:   const result = {
365:     stage: 'dispatch',
366:     id,
367:     publicN,
368:     ok: dispatched.status === 0,
369:     code: dispatched.status,
370:     out: (dispatched.stdout || '').trim().slice(-600),
371:     err: (dispatched.stderr || '').trim().slice(-400),
372:   };
373:   // The notice is reported, never fatal: a card that is filed and dispatched but
374:   // unsent is still filed, and failing the pass here would make the poller re-run
375:   // create/pack against a card that already exists.
376:   if (!has('--quiet-notify')) {
377:     const card = cardLabel(publicN, id);
378:   const n = notifyChat(filedNotice(card, parsed, comment, slug, result, has('--detach')));
379:     result.notified = n.ok;
380:     if (!n.ok) result.notifyWhy = n.why;
381:   }
382:   return result;

387: // WHY TELEGRAM AND NOT THE BUG API
388: // The obvious design was to POST straight to the bug store. That needs a
389: // credential off-box: bugWriteGuard accepts a token, same-origin, or loopback-only
390: // when BUG_API_TOKEN is unset — so a poller anywhere but the app box gets 401, and
391: // withFallback then QUEUES the write, returns queued:true and exits 0. A poller
392: // that cannot reach the store looks exactly like a poller that filed the work.
393: //
394: // The notification route has no such edge. Telegram is outbound-only from here:
395: // the bot's webhook (https://health-tracker.co.uk/tghook/vm) is what receives,
396: // and this site never has to accept a POST. The receiving agent already lives on
397: // the VM, where bugctl works over loopback. So no token is provisioned, nothing
398: // is provisioned, and the human sees the instruction in Telegram — which is the
399: // point of a notification rather than a silent write.

401: // WHY IT MUST BE SENT AS A USER, NOT AS THE BOT

403: // @VM_19485_bot would put the text in the chat and never wake the bot — it would
404: // look like it worked. scripts/lib/tg-userbot.mjs sendAsUser() is the existing
405: // user client; seat-tags.mjs uses the same session for the same reason ("a bot

410: // bot-token path in telegram-send.sh hit exactly that failure and silently fell

- Extract duplicated CLI-arg helpers (`argv`, `has`, `val`) from three tooling scripts into a single shared module `tooling/lib/args.js`, then import it in each script.

## Important Details
- Exact helper definitions (confirmed in `check-contrast.js` lines 28–30, same in the other two):
  - `const argv = process.argv.slice(2);`
  - `const has = f => argv.includes(f);`
